description_full: Galiano Gold Inc. operates as a gold mining company. It owns a 90% interest in the Asanko Gold Mine consists of the Nkran, Esaase, Abore, and Miradani North open-pit mining areas located on the Asankrangwa Gold Belt in the Amansie West District of the Republic of Ghana, West Africa. The company was formerly known as Asanko Gold Inc. and changed its name to Galiano Gold Inc. in April 2020. Galiano Gold Inc. was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: Galiano Gold Inc. is a small-cap basic materials business with a $654M market cap on $448M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -3.5pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 15% against a 10% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 24% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $43M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -31.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
